sentences.text: This claim petition is filed u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a RTA.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 17.02.2024 at about 6.45 p.m, the deceased was walking beside of the road near pump house, Pandithahalli village, Malavalli - Kollegala road,
Mandya District.

At that time the rider of Hero Passion Pro motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-10-EC-5344 came from Malavalli side with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to the deceased.
Due to the impact the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

Immediately he was shifted to Malavalli Government Hospital, and after first aid he was shifted to Mandya Government Hospital, wherein during the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries at hospital.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending 4 SCCH-23 MVC-2136/2024 motorcycle.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle and as such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Contending the above facts, they pray to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement by contending that the petition is not maintainable either law or on facts.

This respondent denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-10-EC-5344 further the Fulvanthi Devi vs Madesh A V on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146253412/

respondent No.2 submitted that the liability of this respondent if any is subject to the terms,
conditions and limitations of the policy of insurance, issued in favour of the alleged owner and in accordance with the provisions of IMV Act.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the 5 SCCH-23 MVC-2136/2024 accident.
Negligence on the part of the rider of offending vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of offending vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the owner of the vehicle, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?

?

4) What order or award?

Perused the entire materials placed on record.

This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following :

sentences.text: The petitioners have knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.50,00,000/- together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint herein, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed 7 SCCH-23 MVC-2136/2024 charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle for the offences punishable under section's 279, 304(A) of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
With this observation issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative.
9. ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioners claim that Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are the minor children and petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief- examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of petitioners and deceased are marked at Ex's.P.11 to 16 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the 8 SCCH-23 MVC-2136/2024 petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE NO.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that deceased was working as coolie and earning Rs.1,000/- per day.
In order to substantiate the above said fact absolutely no string of evidence is produced before this Court.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
9 SCCH-23 MVC-2136/2024 "(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2024.

Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into Fulvanthi Devi vs Madesh A V on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146253412/
4 consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
11.

sentences.text: The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P16 wherein the date of deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1991, which indicates that he was aged (33 years 1 months 16 days) 33 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '16'.
10 SCCH-23 MVC-2136/2024 12.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 33 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 33 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.23,100/- p.m. (Rs.16,500/-
+ 6,600/- i.e. 40%).
13.
The deceased died living behind 5 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.17,325/- p.m. (Rs.23,100 - Rs.5,775 = Rs.17,325/-).
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.17,325/- p.m. and the multiplier '16' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.33,26,400/- (Rs.17,325 X 12 X 16).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.33,26,400/- under the head of loss of dependency.

15. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
16.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are the minor children and the petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the 12 SCCH-23 MVC-2136/2024 case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Fulvanthi Devi vs Madesh A V on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146253412/

sentences.text: 5 Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 5 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her father, as well as Petitioner no.5 towards deceased her son.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

17. The calculation table stands as follows :
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount 1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.33,26,400/-
2. Towards loss of Consortium to Rs. 48,400/-
the petitioner No.1 3.

body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses 5. Towards loss of Filial consortium Rs. 1,60,000/-

13 SCCH-23  MVC-2136/2024 18. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
19. It is contended in para 12 of the written statement that, respondent.No.2 has not issued any policy.

However careful perusal of policy which is found in documents as per the contents of which the POS- Motor Two - Wheelers policy bundled - schedule cum certificate of issuance of insurance policy is respect of motorcycle covering the date of accident (TP- Third Party - From 30.11.2020 to 29.11.2025).
The accident is occurred on 17.02.2024.
Hence, there is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the Hero Passion pro motorcycle thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily 14 SCCH-23 MVC-2136/2024 liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
20. ISSUE NO.4 :

ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

sentences.text: The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.35,71,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 20% Petitioner No.2 - 20% Petitioner No.3 - 20% Petitioner No.4 - 20% Petitioner No.4 - 20% 15 SCCH-23 MVC-2136/2024

Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 & 5 a sum equal to 20% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 80% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 & 5 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 to 4 is ordered to be deposited in their names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority, at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioners.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
